cards.text: Here the prophet is praying for God’s people, and he opens BIG: “I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts,” because of all the many good things the LORD has done for the house of Israel. Friend, this man did not walk in with a sticky note. He walked in with a SCROLL.

cards.question: God said of Israel, “They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal.” So what did He become for them?
When Israel was in distress, the LORD kept His distance from it.

cards.text: In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and compassion He redeemed them.
He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old. Friend, I use my mustache for hands and I STILL drop a cookie box on a good day, and He carried a whole NATION.
Then comes the turn nobody wants. Israel rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit.

cards.question: After Israel rebelled, the LORD turned and became their ___.

cards.text: Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses, Israel’s leader. I know that one, friend: back in the drawer I replayed every batch from the Millers’ counter and wondered where that kitchen light went.

cards.question: Remembering Moses, they ask where the One is who brought them through the ___.

cards.text: Where is the One who set His Holy Spirit among them, who sent His glorious arm to lead them by the right hand of Moses and divided the waters before them? Friend, that’s not one question, that’s a whole LIST, and every item on it is a headline.

cards.question: The prayer gives a reason the LORD divided the waters before His people. What is it?

answers.text: To make His name famous forever
To show Moses was worth following
To teach His people to obey Him

cards.question: The LORD led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, and they kept stumbling the whole way.

cards.text: Like cattle going down to the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest, and the prophet tells the LORD He led His people this way to make for Himself a glorious name. Friend, after a double batch I head for rest too, but less like cattle in a valley and more like a cookie box sliding off the counter.

Then the prayer looks up: “Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation.” Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer hoping somebody would open it and SEE me, so I feel that line all the way down to my gold base.

cards.question: The one praying asks where God’s zeal and might are. What does he say about God’s compassion for him right now?

answers.text: It was given to his enemies

cards.text: Then a hard line: Abraham, the forefather of the nation, does not know them, and Israel, the forefather Jacob (Genesis 32:28), does not acknowledge them. Their own family tree is leaving them on READ.

cards.question: Even so, the prayer tells the LORD that He is their ___, their Redeemer from Everlasting.
The prayer asks the LORD why He makes them stray from His ways and hardens their hearts. Then it asks Him to do something for the sake of His servants. What?
The prayer says God’s people possessed His holy place for only a short while, and now enemies have trampled His sanctuary.

cards.text: Now they say they’ve become like those He never ruled, like those not called by His name. Friend, I think that is the sound of a people who feel FORGOTTEN.
Now the prayer gets LOUD: if only the LORD would rend the heavens and come down, so the mountains would quake at His presence! Friend, this is NOT “call me back when you get a minute.”

cards.question: The prayer says God coming down would be like fire making water boil. Who would it make His name known to?

cards.text: And He’s done it before. When He did awesome works they did not expect, He came down, and the mountains trembled at His presence.

cards.question: The prayer says no eye has ever seen any God besides the LORD, who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him.

cards.text: The LORD welcomes those who gladly do right and remember His ways. Then the prayer comes clean: “Surely You were angry, for we sinned.”

cards.question: Right after admitting they sinned, what does the prayer ask the LORD?

answers.text: How they can be saved if they stay in their sins
Why He ever chose them to be His people
When their enemies will finally leave the land

cards.question: The prayer says their righteous acts are clean enough to make up for their sins.

cards.text: The prayer says each of them has become like something unclean, and all their righteous acts are like filthy rags. Not their WORST stuff, friend, but their BEST stuff.

cards.question: The prayer says no one calls on the LORD’s name or strives to take hold of Him. What does it say the LORD has done with His face?

cards.text: And right in the middle of all that, the prayer turns with “But now, O LORD, You are our Father” and friend, that’s that line again. I think it lands even harder this time.

cards.question: The prayer paints a picture: the people are the clay, and the LORD is the ___.

cards.text: We are all the work of His hand. Friend, every cookie with my stamp on it is MINE, even the lopsided ones I hide in the back of the box.

cards.question: The prayer asks the LORD not to be angry beyond measure, and not to remember their ___ forever.

cards.text: Then the prayer looks around. God’s holy cities have become a wilderness, Zion a wasteland and Jerusalem a desolation.

cards.question: What happened to the holy and beautiful temple where their fathers praised God?

answers.text: It was washed away in a flood
It was taken apart and moved

cards.text: And all that was dear to them lies in ruins. No joke here, friend: this is a people standing in the rubble, still talking to God.

cards.question: The prayer ends by asking whether the LORD will keep silent and afflict them beyond measure.

cards.text: “Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?” That’s where the prayer stops, friend, right on the question.
